wiki_only_topics.topic: Commanders Alexander O'Reilly and John Acton
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: The amphibious assault was led by Spanish general Alexander O'Reilly and Tuscan admiral Sir John Acton, commanding a total of 20,000 men along with 74 warships of various sizes and 230 transport ships carrying the troops for the invasion.

wiki_only_topics.topic: Specific fleet composition and troop numbers
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: By June the task force that had been assembled was enormous, with seven ships of the line, twelve frigates, twenty-seven gunboats, five hulks, nine feluccas, four mortar boats, seven galleys and three smaller warships, along with two hundred and thirty transport ships.

wiki_only_topics.topic: Tactical details of the landing and artillery loss
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: Most of the guns became stuck in the wet sand resulting in their absence from the ensuing fight.

The losses were huge; suffering more than 5,000 casualties, including five generals killed and fifteen wounded (with one of these being Bernado de Galvez), and abandoning to the Algerians no fewer than 15 artillery pieces and some 9000 other weapons.
Despite the failed invasion attempt, in 1780 Spain and Morocco signed a treaty of friendship at the Peace of Aranjuez.
